This package is a Python implementation of the IMF–World Bank **Low-Income Country Debt Sustainability Framework** (LIC-DSF) IDA21 template, vintage **2025-08-12**. It evaluates the same Chart Data surface an economist reads in the Excel workbook: external and public-debt risk ratings, breach flags, tailored-stress applicability, fiscal-space language, and the indicator paths that feed the standard DSA charts.

Install it, then import the public functions from `lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api`:

```bash
uv add lic-dsf-2025-08-12
```

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import api, data
```

The shipped defaults reproduce the template snapshot (country **Ghana**, first projection year **2024**). Each `compute_*` function takes one typed input bundle. `from_defaults()` fills that bundle from the snapshot; override only the fields you would have edited in yellow. `describe()` on any bundle lists its fields, allowed values, defaults, and source cells.

A one-field bundle is enough to ask whether the natural-disaster tailored test applies:

```{python}
api.compute_tailored_stress_natural_disaster_applicable(
    api.TailoredStressNaturalDisasterApplicableInputs.from_defaults(
        country=data.COUNTRY_DEFAULT,
    )
)
```

Most other `compute_*` functions need the full Input 1–8 case. The next page shows how to load the workbook defaults and return the three risk ratings an economist puts at the top of a write-up.

## What this library is for

A typical LIC-DSF exercise in Excel is:

1. Fill **Input 1–8** (country, vintage, debt coverage, macro-debt history, external and domestic financing, stress options, residual financing, SDR) and, if needed, the customized-scenario sheets.
2. Let the engine sheets (`Macro-Debt_Data`, `PV_Base`, `Chart Data`, the stress tabs) calculate.
3. Read **Chart Data**: ratings, breaches, MX-shock labels, tailored-test flags, fiscal space, and the figure/stress-ladder series. The Realism 1–4 and Probability approach sheets publish the companion chart series used by Output 4 and Output 6.

This package exposes step 3 as Python functions. You do not open Excel. You pass a named input bundle (scalars and labeled series) and get back either a scalar or a `Series` keyed by axes such as `SCENARIO` and `TIME_PERIOD`.

Yellow cells on the Input sheets are the economist-facing surface. Green intermediate sheets are not part of the public API.

## Interactive dependency graph

```{=html}
<a
  class="series-graph-preview"
  id="series-graph-preview"
  href="assets/graph/index.html"
  target="_blank"
  rel="noopener"
  aria-label="Open the interactive LIC-DSF dependency graph"
>
  <iframe
    id="series-graph-frame"
    title="LIC-DSF dependency graph preview"
    loading="lazy"
    tabindex="-1"
    aria-hidden="true"
  ></iframe>
  <div class="series-graph-cta">
    <span>Open statement graph</span>
    <span class="hint">Pan · zoom · inspect statements</span>
  </div>
</a>
<script>
(function () {
  var link = document.getElementById("series-graph-preview");
  var frame = document.getElementById("series-graph-frame");
  if (!link || !frame) return;
  // Great Docs publishes the app at site-root assets/graph/.
  var underGuide = /\/user-guide\//.test(location.pathname);
  var bases = underGuide
    ? ["../assets/graph/", "assets/graph/"]
    : ["assets/graph/", "../assets/graph/"];
  function apply(base) {
    link.href = new URL(base + "index.html", document.baseURI).href;
    frame.src = new URL(base + "index.html?preview=1", document.baseURI).href;
  }
  function tryNext(i) {
    if (i >= bases.length) {
      apply(bases[0]);
      return;
    }
    var probe = new URL(bases[i] + "index.html", document.baseURI).href;
    fetch(probe, { method: "GET", cache: "no-store" })
      .then(function (res) {
        if (res.ok) apply(bases[i]);
        else tryNext(i + 1);
      })
      .catch(function () { tryNext(i + 1); });
  }
  tryNext(0);
})();
</script>
```

## How to read this guide

| Page | Use it when you want to… |
| --- | --- |
| [Compute a risk rating](user-guide/compute-a-risk-rating.qmd) | Reproduce Chart Data ratings, breaches, MX labels, and fiscal space |
| [Fill the input sheets](user-guide/fill-the-input-sheets.qmd) | Map Input 1–8 onto input-bundle fields and override defaults |
| [Read the Chart Data](user-guide/read-the-chart-data.qmd) | Pull stress-ladder, figure, realism, and probability series |
| [Stress tests and what-ifs](user-guide/stress-tests-and-what-ifs.qmd) | Toggle tailored tests and change a single assumption |

The function-level contract is in the API reference. A later page, [Excel parity validation](user-guide/excel-parity-validation.qmd), records how this vintage was checked against the workbook formulas.

::: {.callout-note}
The authoritative framework prose remains the IMF Guidance Note PDF. This library implements the **IDA21 template arithmetic** for the 2025-08-12 vintage; it does not replace staff judgment on mechanical vs. final ratings.
:::
